# edgeos_firewall_rule (Resource)

One rule in an IPv4 firewall rule set (`firewall name <ruleset> rule <number>`). The resource owns the attributes below; other options of the rule (for example `time` or `recent`) are left untouched, use `edgeos_config` for those.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "edgeos_firewall_name" "wan_in" {
  name = "WAN_IN"
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_rule" "established" {
  ruleset     = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_in.name
  number      = 10
  action      = "accept"
  description = "Allow established and related"
  state = {
    established = true
    related     = true
  }
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_rule" "invalid" {
  ruleset     = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_in.name
  number      = 20
  action      = "drop"
  description = "Drop invalid state"
  state = {
    invalid = true
  }
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_rule" "web" {
  ruleset     = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_in.name
  number      = 30
  action      = "accept"
  description = "HTTPS to the web server"
  protocol    = "tcp"
  destination = {
    address = "192.168.1.10"
    port    = "443"
  }
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_rule" "ping" {
  ruleset  = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_in.name
  number   = 40
  action   = "accept"
  protocol = "icmp"
  log      = true
  source = {
    address = "198.51.100.0/24"
  }
  icmp = {
    type_name = "echo-request"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) `accept`, `drop`, `reject` or `reject-tcp` (needs `protocol = "tcp"`).
- `number` (Number) Rule number from 1 to 9999. Rules are evaluated in ascending order.
- `ruleset` (String) Name of the rule set, usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `destination` (Attributes) Match on the destination of the packet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination))
- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the rule in the config but switch it off (the `disable` node). Defaults to `false`.
- `icmp` (Attributes) Match ICMP type and code. Needs `protocol = "icmp"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--icmp))
- `log` (Boolean) Log packets matching this rule. Unset leaves the EdgeOS default (no logging).
- `protocol` (String) Protocol name or number, such as `tcp`, `udp`, `tcp_udp`, `icmp` or `all`. Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `source` (Attributes) Match on the source of the packet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))
- `state` (Attributes) Match on connection tracking state. Each attribute set to `true` or `false` writes `enable` or `disable`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--state))
- `tcp_flags` (String) TCP flags to match, such as `SYN,!ACK`. Needs `protocol = "tcp"`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<ruleset>:<number>`.

<a id="nestedatt--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address, network (`192.0.2.0/24`) or range (`192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20`). Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `address_group` (String) Name of a firewall address group to match.
- `network_group` (String) Name of a firewall network group to match.
- `port` (String) Port, range, service name or comma separated list, such as `22`, `8000-8080` or `http,https`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.
- `port_group` (String) Name of a firewall port group to match.


<a id="nestedatt--icmp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `icmp`

Optional:

- `code` (Number) ICMP code number, used together with `type`.
- `type` (Number) ICMP type number.
- `type_name` (String) ICMP type name such as `echo-request`. Conflicts with `type`.


<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address, network (`192.0.2.0/24`) or range (`192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20`). Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `address_group` (String) Name of a firewall address group to match.
- `mac_address` (String) Source MAC address in lower case.
- `network_group` (String) Name of a firewall network group to match.
- `port` (String) Port, range, service name or comma separated list, such as `22`, `8000-8080` or `http,https`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.
- `port_group` (String) Name of a firewall port group to match.


<a id="nestedatt--state"></a>
### Nested Schema for `state`

Optional:

- `established` (Boolean) Match established connections.
- `invalid` (Boolean) Match invalid packets.
- `new` (Boolean) Match new connections.
- `related` (Boolean) Match related connections.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_firewall_rule.established
  id = "WAN_IN:10"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <ruleset>:<number>
terraform import edgeos_firewall_rule.established WAN_IN:10
```
